text: OK # CSV Functions and `$escape` Parameter Deprecation Based on the PHP 8.4 deprecated features documentation, here is the verbatim information about CSV functions: ## Standard Library > Using the default value for the `escape` parameter for the [fputcsv()](function.fputcsv.php), [fgetcsv()](function.fgetcsv.php), and [str_getcsv()](function.str-getcsv.php) is now deprecated. It must be passed explicitly either positionally or via named arguments. ## SPL > Using the default value for the `escape` parameter for the [SplFileObject::setCsvControl()](splfileobject.setcsvcontrol.php), [SplFileObject::fputcsv()](splfileobject.fputcsv.php), and [SplFileObject::fgetcsv()](splfileobject.fgetcsv.php) is now deprecated. It must be passed explicitly either positionally or via named arguments. This does not apply to [SplFileObject::fputcsv()](splfileobject.fputcsv.php) and [SplFileObject::fgetcsv()](splfileobject.fgetcsv.php) if [SplFileObject::setCsvControl()](splfileobject.setcsvcontrol.php) was used to set a new default value. ## Functions Affected - `fputcsv()` - `fgetcsv()` - `str_getcsv()` - `SplFileObject::setCsvControl()` - `SplFileObject::fputcsv()` - `SplFileObject::fgetcsv()` **Note:
